Technology stocks were leading the selloff for U.S. stocks Monday, with shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were losing 3% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was falling 3.7%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Black Box ( BBOX ) raced 22% higher on Monday after it unveiled a definitive merger deal with AGC Networks Pte. Ltd., the Singaporean subsidiary of global solutions integrator AGC Networks Ltd., under which AGC will acquire the IT infrastructure products and services company. Under the deal, an indirect wholly owned US subsidiary of AGC will initiate a tender offer to purchase all of the outstanding shares of Black Box common stock for $1.08 per share in cash.
In other sector news:
(+) Apptio ( APTI ) jumped 51% on Monday after agreeing to an all-cash $1.94 billion buyout led by an affiliate of Vista Equity Partners. Under terms of the proposed offer, Vista will pay $38 for each Apptio share, representing a 53% premium to Friday's closing price. Apptio, which helps customers manage, plan and optimize their investments, also has a 30-day "go-shop" to actively solicit and potentially enter negotiations for alternative buyout proposals.
(-) SAP ( SAP ) declined as much as 6% on Monday after the German software giant said it was acquiring Qualtrics International for $8 billion in cash. SAP said it is expecting the acquisition will help bolster its experience management offering and help customers to better manage supply chains, networks, employees and core processes.
